questions.q: Which package would you import each from: a type guard like isEmail, and the branded type UserId?
questions.explain: Guards, converters, utility types, Clock and Random are in @zudojs/types. Branded ids and their factories, and the shared constants, are in @zudojs/constants.

questions.q: What makes function isPaymentEvent(value: unknown): value is PaymentEvent a type guard?
questions.explain: The guard checks at runtime and narrows at compile time. It changes nothing about the value; it only proves something about it.
options: It throws when the value is invalid
Its return type value is PaymentEvent tells TypeScript to treat value as a PaymentEvent wherever the function returned true
It converts the value into a PaymentEvent

questions.q: Why is typeof body === "object" not enough to check a JSON request body?
questions.explain: isPlainObject accepts only plain objects (including null-prototype ones) and refuses null, arrays and instances such as new Date().
options: It is also true for null, arrays and class instances
It is false for objects created by JSON.parse
It only works in the browser

questions.q: Which check is right for an amount in kobo from a webhook?
questions.explain: Kobo amounts are whole and positive. typeof accepts NaN and Infinity, isFiniteNumber accepts -100 and 2.5, and Number(x) turns the string "250000" into a number instead of refusing it.

questions.q: Why does isArrayOfType read every index instead of using Array.prototype.every?
questions.explain: A sparse array has no elements at the empty indexes, and every never calls its callback for them. Reading each index tests a hole as undefined.
options: every skips holes, so new Array(3) would pass any element check
every does not exist on typed arrays

questions.q: When should you prefer a @zudojs/schema schema over hand-written guards?
questions.explain: Guards are the building blocks and fit small checks. A schema composes checks, reports every failing path, and gives you the type with Infer.
options: For whole request bodies, where you want error messages for every field and a TypeScript type from one declaration

questions.q: ?pageSize= arrives empty. What does toNumber(query.get("pageSize"), 20) return, and why is that better than Number(...)?
questions.explain: Number("") is 0, which quietly turns into a page size, a price or a limit. toNumber treats blank text as "not given".
options: 20: blank strings fall back instead of silently becoming 0

questions.q: What does safeJsonParse<Order>(text, fallback) guarantee?
questions.explain: "Safe" means no exception and no prototype-polluting keys. Validate the result with guards or a schema before trusting its shape.
options: That the result is a valid Order
That broken JSON gives the fallback and that __proto__, constructor and prototype keys are dropped; the result is only cast to Order, not checked
That numbers are converted to strings

questions.q: Why are __proto__ keys dangerous even though JSON.parse keeps them as ordinary properties?
questions.explain: This is prototype pollution: one request could add, say, isAdmin: true to every object. Dropping the keys at parse time removes the risk for everything downstream.
options: A later deep merge that walks into __proto__ can change Object.prototype for the whole process

questions.q: What does DeepReadonly<ShopSettings> do at runtime?
questions.explain: Types are erased when TypeScript compiles. Pair the type with Object.freeze (deeply, for nested objects) when the data truly must not change.
options: Nothing: it only makes the compiler refuse changes at every depth; use Object.freeze for runtime protection

questions.q: Why does cancelOrder(userId, orderId) compile when both parameters are string, and how does a brand fix it?
questions.explain: A brand like string & { readonly __brand: "OrderId" } exists only for the compiler. At runtime the id is still a plain string.
options: TypeScript ignores parameter order; brands add runtime checks
TypeScript compares structure, and every string fits every string parameter; a brand adds a compile-time-only property that makes UserId and OrderId incompatible
Strings are always any; brands turn them into objects

questions.q: What does createUserId("") return?
questions.explain: Only some factories validate (createTenantId, createTimestamp, createEmailAddress, createUrl and the encoded-string ones). Check the format yourself before branding an id from outside.
options: An empty string branded as UserId: the id factories only brand

questions.q: Where should as OrderId appear in a well-built code base?
questions.explain: A brand is a promise. Making it in one checked place keeps the promise true, and the rest of the code can rely on it without re-checking.
options: Wherever a string needs to become an order id
In one parse function that checks the value first, so every OrderId means "checked at the boundary"

questions.q: Why does createTenantId(" Shop-NG ") return "shop-ng" instead of refusing it?
questions.explain: A tenant id ends up in cache keys, log lines and paths. Normalising first, and refusing separators like /, closes a whole class of isolation bugs.
options: It normalises (trims, lowercases, Unicode-normalises) so two spellings of one tenant cannot become two tenants, then validates the result
Tenant ids are case-insensitive in every database

questions.q: A request timed out and you do not know whether the server handled it. Which methods may a client safely send again?
questions.explain: An idempotent request has the same effect whether it arrives once or twice. Repeating a payment POST can charge twice, which is what idempotency keys prevent.
options: The ones in IDEMPOTENT_HTTP_METHODS, such as GET, PUT and DELETE; not POST or PATCH

questions.q: What is the main benefit of HttpHeader.CONTENT_TYPE over typing "Content-Type"?
questions.explain: HTTP header names are case-insensitive on the wire, but a misspelt name is a different header. The constant turns that typo into a compiler error.
options: Header names are case-sensitive, so the constant is required
A typo in the constant's name is a compile error, and a search finds every use

questions.q: A server is deployed with NODE_ENV=prodution. What does resolveEnvironment() do, and how do you make it fail instead?
questions.explain: The lenient default keeps local tools running. A deploy check with strict: true stops a typo from running a development configuration in production.
options: Falls back to development with a one-time warning; pass { strict: true } to throw InvalidConstantError

questions.q: With NODE_ENV=staging, what are resolveEnvironment() and isProduction()?
questions.explain: staging is one of the four environments. Code that must behave like production in staging should check for both, not rely on isProduction.

questions.q: Why is formatDuration fine for logs but not for an invoice line "Parking: 1h 59m 59s"?
questions.explain: Two rounded-down units are readable in a log. Billing needs exact values computed from the milliseconds.
options: It shows at most two units and rounds down, so 1h 59m 59s prints as "1h 59m"
It uses the local time zone

questions.q: Why does OrderService take a Clock in its constructor instead of calling Date.now()?
questions.explain: Injecting time turns it from a hidden global into a parameter the test controls. The same goes for randomness.
options: A test can pass a FixedClock and check "31 minutes later" instantly and exactly

questions.q: A service computes createdAt and payBy with two separate clock.now() calls. Why did the FixedClock tests pass while production showed 1,800,002 ms instead of 30 minutes?
questions.explain: Controlled test doubles hide some bugs. Read time once and derive every related value from that reading, and keep one test with the real clock.
options: A fixed clock returns the same time on every call, so the tests could not see that two readings differ; read the clock once per operation
Timestamps lose precision when converted to strings

questions.q: Why can't you pass new SeededRandom(1) to a function that takes Random?
questions.explain: Anyone who knows the seed can predict every value. The compiler error keeps test generators away from tokens and session ids.
options: Random carries a hidden brand that only secure generators have, so a predictable generator cannot reach code that makes secrets
It works; it is only a warning

questions.q: You import systemClock from @zudojs/constants and call systemClock.now(), but pass it to code expecting the @zudojs/types Clock. What should you know?
questions.explain: Both packages export a systemClock and a systemRandom. The @zudojs/types versions are the ones the framework is moving to.
options: They are different objects with different interfaces (constants adds Date(), its Random has other methods); prefer the @zudojs/types ones

questions.q: What does using new SeededRandom(42) in a test give you?
questions.explain: Determinism is the point. Change the seed and the expected values change with it; keep it fixed in the test.
options: The same sequence of ids on every run and every machine, so tests can compare and snapshot them

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Arrays and class instances are not plain objects. Infinity is not finite, 0 is not positive, and the string "3" is not an integer.
options:
true false false false
false false true false

true true false false
false true true true

true false true false
false false true false

true false false false
true false true true

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The date guards check the calendar (no 30 February) and accept numeric offsets. isIsoDateTimeString requires a time. new Date("tomorrow") is an Invalid Date, which isDate refuses.
options:
true false false
true false true

true true false
true true true

true false true
false false true

true false false
false false false

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Blank text, hexadecimal and trailing junk all fall back; surrounding spaces are fine. Number("0x1A") would be 26 and parseInt("12kg") 12, which is exactly what the converter refuses.
questions.code:
import { toNumber } from "@zudojs/types";

console.log(toNumber("25"), toNumber("", 10), toNumber("0x1A", -1), toNumber("12kg", -1), toNumber(" 7 "));

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Known words convert (case-insensitively); anything else is the fallback, false unless you pass another one.
questions.code:
import { toBoolean } from "@zudojs/types";

console.log(["yes", "off", "1", "maybe", "TRUE"].map((v) => toBoolean(v)).join(" "), toBoolean("maybe", true));
options: true false true false true true
true true true true true true
true false true false false true
true false false false true false

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Acronyms stay one word and leading capitals produce no leading separator, so the results are usable column and file names.
questions.code:
import { camelToKebab, camelToSnake, snakeToCamel } from "@zudojs/types";

console.log(camelToSnake("totalKobo"), camelToSnake("HTTPStatusCode"), snakeToCamel("paid_at"), camelToKebab("OrderItems"));

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Dangerous keys are dropped at every depth, and broken JSON returns the fallback instead of throwing.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: createUserId only brands, spaces and all. The tenant id is normalised to lowercase. April has 30 days, so the timestamp is refused.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: 429 is a client error (the client sent too many requests); 503 is a server error. DELETE changes data, so it is not safe, but deleting twice has the same effect as once, so it is idempotent. PATCH is neither guaranteed.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Aliases and capitalisation are understood; an unknown value falls back to development (quietly, here). isProduction resolves the same way.
questions.code:
import { isProduction, resolveEnvironment } from "@zudojs/constants";

console.log(resolveEnvironment({ NODE_ENV: "PROD" }), resolveEnvironment({ NODE_ENV: "dev" }), resolveEnvironment({ NODE_ENV: "qa" }, { silent: true }), isProduction({ NODE_ENV: "prod" }));

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: 3,725,000 ms is 1 h 2 min 5 s, shown as two units, rounded down. 59,999 ms rounds down to 59 s, not up to a minute.
questions.code:
import { TimeMs, formatDuration, toMilliseconds } from "@zudojs/constants";

console.log(toMilliseconds(2, "hours") === 2 * TimeMs.HOUR, formatDuration(3_725_000), formatDuration(59_999), formatDuration(999));

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: advance moves the clock 45 minutes, across midnight and into February. Month numbers in Date.UTC start at 0, so 0 is January.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Same seed, same sequence; a different seed gives different values. deterministic marks the generator as a test double. custom(4, …) returns 4 characters from the alphabet.

questions.q: Write problems(value) for a cart line { sku, qty, unitKobo }: return ["(not an object)"] for anything that is not a plain object, otherwise the list of failing fields: sku must be a non-empty string, qty an integer from 1 to 99, unitKobo a positive integer. Use @zudojs/types.
questions.explain: Checking every field and reporting all failures at once saves the client a round trip per mistake. After isPlainObject, TypeScript lets you read value.sku as unknown, and each guard narrows it.

questions.q: Write parseInvoiceId(value: unknown): InvoiceId, where InvoiceId is Brand<string, "InvoiceId">. Accept only strings like INV-2026-000123 (the letters INV, a 4-digit year, 6 digits); throw Error("Not an invoice id: …") with the JSON of the value otherwise.
questions.explain: Check first, brand second, in one place. JSON.stringify in the message shows the value's type too: "123" and 123 look different.
questions.expected:
ok INV-2026-000123
Not an invoice id: "INV-26-123"
Not an invoice id: "inv-2026-000123"
Not an invoice id: 123

questions.q: Write readListQuery(search) for ?page=&pageSize=&inStock=: page defaults to 1 and pageSize to 20 (use toNumber), pageSize is clamped to at most 100 (Limits.MAX_PAGE_SIZE), and inStock uses toBoolean with fallback false.
questions.explain: Fallbacks handle missing and blank values; the clamp stops a client from asking for 5,000 rows at once. A real endpoint would also refuse a page below 1.

questions.q: Write createOtpService(clock) with issue() (stores the issue time and returns it) and isValid(issuedAt) (true for less than 5 minutes). Test at 0, 4 and 5 minutes with a FixedClock.
questions.explain: The boundary at exactly 5 minutes is the interesting case, and only a controllable clock can put a test exactly there.
questions.expected:
0 min: true
4 min: true
5 min: false

questions.q: Write createOrderIds(source) that returns a function producing "ord_" + source.uuid(). Type source so that both systemRandom and a SeededRandom are accepted, and show that two generators with seed 3 produce the same first id.
questions.explain: Order ids are identifiers, not secrets, so the function accepts either kind of generator. A function that makes secrets would take Random only.

questions.q: Write describeStatus(code) using isSuccessStatus, isRedirectStatus, isClientError and isServerError. Return "retry later" for 429 and 503 (use HttpStatus), otherwise "ok", "redirect", "fix the request" or "server problem".
questions.explain: The special cases come first: 429 is a client error by class, but the right reaction is to wait and retry, the same as for 503.
questions.expected: ok | redirect | fix the request | retry later | server problem | retry later

questions.q: Fix place so it reads the clock once: payBy must be exactly 30 minutes after createdAt even with a clock that moves on every call.
questions.explain: A ticking test clock exposes what a fixed one hides. One reading per operation keeps related times consistent.
